_deal: The board's test node, until he plays it.
author: jessica
source: his Trello "Discover Faint signal", proposed 2026-10-31 08:11 as a family; his "yeah Faint signal sounds good" 08:15

place._theme: Any built site that is not a cave or a natural landmark: somewhere a beacon could be.

prose.name: Survey: Faint Signal on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The comms office has picked up a faint signal from the <Place> and wants someone to go and find out what's sending it.
prose.card: Comms Office Contract. A faint signal is coming from the <Place> on <Planet>. Find its source. Payment on completion.

_note: FAINT SIGNAL: a new board family, his Trello card. Every letter has the SAME card, title and first journal, so the board never says which one he has drawn; what changes is what is at the source. The broadcast is the signal itself, heard on arrival.
⛔ FAMILY RULE: no letter's broadcast may hint at what the source is (card 20261031-080934): the survivor, the loop, the coffee and the bait must all sound like someone who wants to be found.

The source is a placed beacon (outpost beacon01, Overtime's own, on 7 recipes; Satellite_Beacon is ruled out on land). Voices borrowed until his ear casts them. No names, places or currency in any voiced line.
LETTER a: A SURVIVOR: someone kept a beacon on for nine days after the others left to find help.

FAMILY RULE, REFINED 2026-10-31 on the four verdicts: a broadcast may say what KIND of message it is (c's 'supply request', b's all-clear) but not what the source is; and a repeat player may recognise a letter by its call, which is answered by adding letters, not by blanking calls.

FRANCES 2026-10-31 (reviews/2026-10-31-delve-MB92a.md): rework, findings 1-4 and 6 taken, 5 kept as allowed. Forced pick answered YES: the broadcast is a message she recorded once and left looping, nine days old when he hears it; 'I've listened to it long enough' is her own voice on repeat.

beats.objective: Find the source of the signal at the <Place>
beats.name: Signal Beacon

message.title: Signal Beacon
message.text: The beacon's battery light is nearly out. Someone is waiting beside it.

beats.journal: The signal comes from a beacon at the <Place>, and someone is sitting beside it. I should talk to them.

beats.objective: Talk to the survivor at the <Place>
beats.journal: I found the source of the signal: a survivor who kept a beacon running for nine days. I've called in help for her.
greeting: You heard it. I'd stopped believing anyone would. The others took the ship to find help on the first morning, and I've been sitting by that beacon for nine days.

exchanges.prompt: Help's coming. I'll call it in.
reply: Then I'm turning that beacon off. I've listened to it long enough.

exchanges.prompt: Nine days is a long time to sit and wait.
reply: It takes counting. I counted everything I could see, twice, and then I started again.

exchanges.prompt: Why didn't you go with them?
reply: Someone had to keep the beacon on. And I'm a terrible pilot.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 is the hand-back: it ends the conversation and pays 'reward'. Every prompt rests on the greeting.

broadcast: If anyone can hear this, I'm still here.
_speech: The signal itself, heard on arrival. Its subtitle name differs per letter (SPEAKER rule) without saying what the source is.
